ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in a uniform magnetic field there are two conducting circular rings a and b, and the direction of the magnetic field is perpendicular to the plane in which the circular rings lie. The magnetic induction intensity B increases uniformly with time. The ratio of the radii of the two circular rings is 2∶1, and the induced electromotive forces produced in the circular rings are respectively Ea and Eb. The mutual influence between the two circular rings is not considered. Which of the following statements is correct? (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: Ea∶Eb=4∶1, the induced currents are both in the clockwise direction

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, in a uniform magnetic field there are two conducting circular rings a and b, and the direction of the magnetic field is perpendicular to the plane in which the circular rings lie. The magnetic induction intensity B increases uniformly with time. The ratio of the radii of the two circular rings is 2∶1, and the induced electromotive forces produced in the circular rings are respectively Ea and Eb. The mutual influence between the two circular rings is not considered. Find the ratio of the induced electromotive forces produced in the two circular rings, Ea∶Eb.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there are many uniformly distributed black dots representing the same uniform magnetic field, and the magnetic field is perpendicular to the plane in which the circular rings lie; on the left is the larger conducting circular ring a, and on the right is the smaller conducting circular ring b; both are in this magnetic field and are separated from each other. The problem text gives that the ratio of the radii of the two circular rings is ra:rb=2:1, the magnetic induction intensity B increases uniformly with time, and the mutual influence between the two circular rings is not considered. Reasoning: For any circular ring, the magnetic flux Φ=B·S=Bπr². According to Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, the magnitude of the induced electromotive force is E=|dΦ/dt|=πr²·|dB/dt|. The two circular rings are in the same uniform magnetic field, and dB/dt is the same, so the ratio of the induced electromotive forces is only equal to the ratio of the areas: Ea:Eb=πra²:πrb²=ra²:rb²=2²:1²=4:1.
